verdict.reasoning: Patient says he has 'not been well for a good few days,' feels 'a bit run down,' and reports 'a cough, a cold'; timing clarified as starting Saturday, five days before Wednesday. He also reports a sore throat.
Patient states cough is 'mostly dry' and 'in the morning, it's a bit worse,' and later acknowledges 'a wee bit' of phlegm.

Patient explicitly links hoarseness to 'watching the football' and says 'I've been shouting myself a wee bit hoarse because the performance has been pretty shy.'

When asked about ears, patient says 'Yeah, yeah, a wee bit... my hearing's... not as good as it used to be, but... I think it's all right,' which supports a mild ear symptom though not severe pain; described in note as mild dull/blocked sensation.

Doctor asks if he feels 'more breathless,' patient answers 'It's not good' and agrees he is 'feeling more short of breath'; he denies chest pain: 'it's just a wee bit shortness of breath, but it's not pain.'

Patient reports feeling hot/cold and sweaty in bed needing to remove and replace blankets, and states he has not used a thermometer: 'I just feel it on my forehead... [haven’t] used a thermometer.' Night sweating implies nocturnal sweating with subjective fever.
Patient says 'The first day I had... a wee bit of... diarrhea, you know, but that's fine now,' indicating day-one diarrhea now resolved.
When asked about appetite, patient says 'I think my appetite's been all right... Fluids up as well,' indicating eating and drinking okay.
Patient describes 'just a wee bit stiffer than normal' in elbows and knees 'when I'm bending down and moving about,' consistent with myalgias/arthralgias/general stiffness.
Symptom onset: 'It would have been Saturday because I was out... for my wife's... celebration... I remember saying to her... I'm not feeling great.'
When asked about travel, patient says 'No, I haven't been' abroad recently.
Patient says 'I've got the diabetes'; later clarified as 'It's a type 2.'

Patient self-describes: 'I'm a wee bit on the chunky side... I've got a wee bit around the midriff. The spare tire's definitely there,' consistent with being overweight.
Patient lists 'metformin' as a regular medication and doctor confirms 'That's correct.'
Patient attempts to name 'another one,' and doctor says '...listen up real, yeah, that sounds like—' indicating lisinopril (phonetic). Thus lisinopril as the second medication is supported.
Patient says he takes 'a wee bit of Aspen or whatever every now and again, but... not... long term,' i.e., occasional aspirin.
Doctor proposes 'a script for antibiotics' to use in 'the next 24 to 48 hours if your symptoms don't get better,' specifying 'something like amoxicillin, one tablet, three times a day.'
Doctor advises if feeling hot/cold and sweaty, 'Taking regular paracetamol would be beneficial,' which applies to fever/aches as needed.
There is no statement about continuing usual medications; metformin and lisinopril are listed but no explicit plan regarding their continuation is discussed.

Patient says he works in 'a wee factory just down the road... we just manufacture... steel parts.'

Regarding smoking, patient says 'Every now and again, but I'm trying to cut that down,' indicating occasional smoking.
